extracted.intended_audience: literate early-18th-century English readers; theatre-goers, periodical readers interested in manners, taste, and moral commentary
extracted.subtask_description: Short periodical essays giving critical guidance on theatrical staging, literary taste, social manners, and moral behaviour for a general literate public; combines theatre criticism with moralizing observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing shadows and realities on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Shadows and Realities ought not to be mix'd together in the same Piece; Scenes, which are designed as the Representations of Nature, should be filled with Resemblances, and not with the Things themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine painted/representational scenery with real objects or animals in a way that creates inconsistency or ridicule (example: drawing a wide champaign country and then crowding the stage with real sheep and oxen). Such mixtures are joining together inconsistencies and make the decoration partly real and partly imaginary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid childish or absurd stage decorations
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be nothing in the Scenes and Machines which may appear Childish and Absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an opera's design is to gratify the senses lavishly, common sense requires it to avoid spectacles that provoke laughter by their absurdity (examples given: Nicolini exposed to a tempest in robes of ermine on a paste-board sea; painted dragons spitting wildfire; enchanted chariots drawn by inappropriate horses). Directors and admirers should keep extravagant effects from descending into the ridiculous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use representations rather than literal duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: If one would represent a wide Champain Country filled with Herds and Flocks, it would be ridiculous to draw the Country only upon the Scenes, and to crowd several Parts of the Stage with Sheep and Oxen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing nature on stage, rely on theatrical resemblance and suggestion rather than attempting literal replication that breaks theatrical illusion and invites ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid theatrical deception that undermines authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not deceive the audience by presenting a thing as actually performing when the effect is produced elsewhere (the sparrows flew in sight, but the music proceeded from a consort of flageolets and bird-calls planted behind the scenes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tricks that simulate life (e.g., live birds 'singing' while music comes from hidden musicians) are akin to comic impostures and may disappoint or betray the audience; authenticity of presentation matters for critical taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage safety and risk for spectacular effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When thunder, lightning, illuminations, and fireworks are used, ensure precautions (there are engines filled with water ready to play at a minute's warning) and prudent management (insure the house).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectacular stage effects must be accompanied by practical safety measures and risk management (e.g., water-engines on standby, insurance) to protect audience and property; theatrical daring does not excuse negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain plausibility and coherence of characters/actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters' capacities and roles should cohere (e.g., puzzlement at an Amazonian Enchantress versed in the Black Art, or a Christian conjuror dealing with the Devil).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incongruities between a character's identity and the actions or skills attributed to them; implausible characterizations invite criticism and undermine the piece's dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer substance and true poetic excellence to florid tinsel
rubrics_metrics.description: One Verse in Virgil is worth all the Clincant or Tinsel of Tasso; modern Italians use a florid, tedious circumlocution and poor imaginations—we should value substantive expression over pompous, weak conceits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism of style: value concise, powerful authority (classical substance) over ornate but vacuous rhetoric; avoid adopting florid circumlocutions that mask poverty of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: When addressing women, refine rather than debase the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is a Woman's Day, in my Works, I shall endeavour at a Stile and Air suitable to their Understanding. Discourse for their Entertainment, is not to be debased but refined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tone and manner to the audience (here: 'reasonable Women') without lowering the subject matter; aim to exalt topics and provide 'tea-table talk'—entertaining yet dignified material appropriate to the audience's understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve privacy of lovers' intimacies but expose falsehood
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall never betray what the Eyes of Lovers say to each other in my Presence. At the same Time I shall not think myself obliged by this Promise, to conceal any false Protestations which I observe made by Glances in publick Assemblies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise discretion: do not reveal genuine private intimacies witnessed in public, but do critique and expose insincere behaviour or false protestations observed in public settings; use observation to show conduct as it aligns with hearts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wit and learning for virtuous ends, not to humour vice
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a mighty Dishonour and Shame to employ excellent Faculties and abundance of Wit, to humour and please Men in their Vices and Follies. The Purpose of a man who appears in Publick ought to be to rescue the Muses out of the Hands of Ravishers, to restore them to their sweet and chaste Mansions, and to engage them in an Employment suitable to their Dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public writers and men of talent should apply their faculties toward improving morals and public good rather than refining or celebrating vice; polish of understanding without good manners is inexcusable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge merit by application to virtue, not mere display of wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitting Wit and Learning as Merit in themselves, without considering the Application of them, leads to degeneracy; it becomes a Rule not so much to regard what we do, as how we do it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works and persons by how abilities are used (their tendency toward public good, justice, piety) rather than by surface elegance or fashionable grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject superstition and avoid multiplying imaginary evils
rubrics_metrics.description: We turn the most indifferent Circumstances into Misfortunes... There is nothing so inconsiderable which may not appear dreadful to an Imagination that is filled with Omens and Prognosticks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason is the means to retrench life's evils; do not give in to omens, prognosticks, or groundless prodigies that create needless fears and additional sorrows (examples: fear of the number thirteen, salt dropped, crickets, screech-owls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not anticipate joys or sorrows; trust providence for fortitude
rubrics_metrics.description: I would not anticipate the Relish of any Happiness, nor feel the Weight of any Misery, before it actually arrives... When I lay me down to Sleep, I recommend my self to his Care; when I awake, I give my self up to his Direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spiritual/moral guidance: avoid pre-experiencing future happiness or misery; cultivate trust in divine governance to fortify against gloomy presages and anxieties about the future.
